AMZN.reasoning: All 5 strategy agents return neutral — this is not a split vote, it is unanimous disciplined abstention from every analytical lens. The underlying trend is real and powerful: EMA alignment is clean (10 EMA $261.20 > 21 EMA $250.05 > 50 EMA $235.75), ADX 65.1 confirms extreme trend strength, and price closed at $272.05 after bulls absorbed and broke above the $268-276 distribution zone that stopped out the prior short on May 4. However, no agent finds a valid entry from current levels. Trend-momentum requires a pullback to the 10 EMA zone ($261-265) before a valid continuation entry exists — price is 4.15% above the 10 EMA with no pullback trigger. Mean-reversion cannot fade (no reversal candle, prior short thesis already stopped out — repeating the same fade without new evidence is disqualified by strategy rules) and cannot dip-buy (no Fibonacci retracement in progress; nearest 23.6% fib is $257.94). Breakout has no setup (BB width 0.2413 already expanded, ADX 65.1 is trending not coiling, volume 0.96x not 1.5x, no confirmed close above $276 resistance). Catalyst-news is neutral (Q1 earnings fully absorbed; next binary Q2 earnings is July 30, ~60 trading days out; Amazon Ads Upfront May 11 is a soft showcase event, not a binary). Macro-context acknowledges bulls have short-term control but flags a transitional rather than clean risk-on regime (Iran-Strait of Hormuz unresolved, oil above $102, hawkish Warsh Fed succession risk May 15) and explicitly states asymmetry from $272 is conditional on clearing $276 — which has not yet been confirmed. Wiki memory reinforces the neutral stance: the AMZN short stopped out at $276 on May 4 (-$7.00), the prior NVDA EMA-pullback setup stopped out at RSI 81-87 (-$63.20), and the Patterns table shows 0% win rate on EMA pullback setups in the last 30 days. Two consecutive stop-outs in RSI 80+/ADX 60+ environments is an explicit pattern-flag against new entries in the same overbought regime without fresh confirmation. No open AMZN position exists (short was stopped out May 4). Portfolio is net 3 long / 3 short across 5 open positions — no stacking concern either direction, but also no capital pressure to deploy here. Actionable conditions to re-evaluate: BULLISH — pullback to 10 EMA zone $258-265 with RSI normalizing below 65 and constructive daily candle on rising ADX; BREAKOUT LONG — confirmed daily close above $276 on volume 1.5x+; BEARISH — hourly RSI >75 plus volume-confirmed rejection candle at $273-276 (neither condition is met today, hourly RSI-21 only 67.45, hourly relative volume 0.04x).
AMZN.key_conflicts: There are no directional conflicts — all 5 agents are neutral. The more important internal tension is the bullish-vs-bearish tilt across agents: swing_trend_momentum and swing_breakout identify the trend as structurally bullish (ADX 65.1, clean EMA alignment, higher highs/higher lows) and would be buyers on a pullback, while swing_mean_reversion and swing_macro_context are wary of the extreme overbought readings (RSI-14 80.49, RSI-21 90.43, z-score 2.06, price 20.36% above 50-SMA) and the prior short stop-out pattern. swing_catalyst_news sits independently neutral: the earnings catalyst has been absorbed and there is no fresh binary event in the next 10 trading days. The productive information in this disagreement: the trend-momentum and breakout agents are telling us the underlying move is legitimate (bulls absorbed supply, not distribution failing), while mean-reversion and macro are telling us the trade has run its primary distance and entry here would be chasing at poor risk/reward with extreme statistics. Together, these views converge on the same practical conclusion: wait for either a clean dip to the 10 EMA ($258-265) or a volume-confirmed breakout above $276 before acting. The macro context carries veto-eligible weight given the geopolitical left-tail (Strait of Hormuz / oil above $102) but does not need to exercise a veto since the other agents are already neutral. The only mild divergence is confidence weighting: swing_catalyst_news (72) and swing_macro_context (62) are more confident in their neutrality than swing_trend_momentum (30), swing_mean_reversion (20), and swing_breakout (20) — the latter three are low-confidence because their frameworks want to act but lack a valid setup, not because they are uncertain about direction.
